title: The reduced geometric fibre locus commutes with base change
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ and $g:T\prime\to T$ be arbitrary morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Put $X\prime=X\times_TT\prime$ and let $f\prime:X\prime\to T\prime$ be the base change of $f$ [def-pc-base-change]. For $t\in T$ and $t\prime\in T\prime$, use geometric fibres over chosen algebraic closures of the respective residue fields [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Then, as subsets of $T\prime$, $$\{t\prime\in T\prime\mid X\prime_{\bar t\prime}\text{ is reduced}\}=g^{-1}\bigl(\{t\in T\mid X_{\bar t}\text{ is reduced}\}\bigr).$$ Here reduced means that every local ring has no nonzero nilpotents [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Empty fibres are included; no flatness, finite-presentation or surjectivity assumption on either morphism is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0576 (lemma-base-change-fibres-geometrically-reduced); its proof applies varieties.tex Tag 0384 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-upstairs) to the residue-field extension. Formulation via reduced geometric fibres uses varieties.tex Tag 035X (lemma-geometrically-reduced), (2) iff (6), in positive characteristic and Tag 020I (lemma-perfect-reduced) in characteristic zero.

proof.text: Fix $t'\in T'$ and put $t=g(t')$, $k=\kappa(t)$, $L=\kappa(t')$. The residue-field map in [def-weil-residue-field] makes $L$ an extension of $k$. Put $Y=X_t$ using [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and write $E=\overline{k}$, $F=\overline{L}$. By [def-weil-geometric-fibre], $X_{\bar t}=Y\times_k\operatorname{Spec}E$ and $X'_{\bar t'}\cong Y\times_k\operatorname{Spec}F$. For the latter identification, the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] says that a morphism into $(X\times_TT')\times_{T'}\operatorname{Spec}F$ is a pair of maps into $X$ and $\operatorname{Spec}F$ agreeing in $T$: its map into $T'$ is forced by $\operatorname{Spec}F\to T'$. The same pair specifies a map into $X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}F$, or into $(X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}k)\times_k\operatorname{Spec}F$, because $\operatorname{Spec}F\to T$ factors through $\operatorname{Spec}k$. These identifications preserve all projections.

source.place: Tag 0576 (lemma-base-change-fibres-geometrically-reduced), first sentence of proof; fibre-product universal property, Tag 01JP

proof.text: Regard $E$ and $F$ as extensions of $k$, with $k\to F$ the composite $k\to L\to F$. Apply [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] to obtain a field $M$ and embeddings $E\to M$, $F\to M$ agreeing on $k$. Both $E$ and $F$ are perfect: in characteristic $p>0$, every $a$ has a $p$-th root because $Z^p-a$ has a root by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; in characteristic zero this is the other case of the definition of perfectness. The field $M$ is reduced, since a nonzero nilpotent in a field would become $1=0$ on multiplication by a power of its inverse.

Choose an affine open cover $Y=\bigcup_i U_i$, $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. For $H=E,F,M$, [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] identifies the inverse image of $U_i$ in $Y_H$ with $U_i\times_k\operatorname{Spec}H$; [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies this open with $\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\otimes_kH)$. The inverse images cover $Y_H$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff] and [def-pc-reduced-scheme] give: $Y_H$ is reduced if and only if every $A_i\otimes_kH$ is reduced. Indeed reducedness of $Y_H$ gives reducedness on its open subschemes by the local-ring definition; conversely every point lies in one of these reduced opens and has the same local ring there.

Assume $X_{\bar t}$ is reduced. For every $i$, step 3 gives that $B_i=A_i\otimes_kE$ is reduced. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-reduced-tensor] over the perfect field $E$ to the reduced $E$-algebras $B_i$ and $M$. It follows that $B_i\otimes_EM$ is reduced. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] this ring is $C_i=A_i\otimes_kM$. More explicitly, after exchanging the two tensor factors by $a\otimes h\mapsto h\otimes a$, the cancellation map is $m\otimes(e\otimes a)\mapsto me\otimes a$, and its inverse is $m\otimes a\mapsto m\otimes(1\otimes a)$; both preserve multiplication. Thus each $C_i$ is reduced.

Put $D_i=A_i\otimes_kF$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat], applied to $M/F$ and $D_i$, the map $D_i\to D_i\otimes_FM$ is faithfully flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] with $R=N=D_i$ and $S=D_i\otimes_FM$: under $D_i\otimes_{D_i}S\cong S$, $d\otimes s\mapsto ds$, it says this ring map is injective. The cancellation isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] identifies $S$ with the reduced ring $C_i$ of step 4, by $(a\otimes f)\otimes m\mapsto a\otimes fm$. If $d^n=0$ in $D_i$, its image in $C_i$ is nilpotent and hence zero, and injectivity forces $d=0$. Therefore every $D_i$ is reduced; by steps 1 and 3, $X'_{\bar t'}$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 00HI (lemma-flat-base-change), faithful field extension; Tag 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective); Tag 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule)

proof.text: Conversely assume $X'_{\bar t'}$ is reduced. Then every $D_i=A_i\otimes_kF$ is reduced by steps 1 and 3. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-reduced-tensor] over the perfect field $F$ to $D_i$ and the field $M$: it gives that $D_i\otimes_FM$ is reduced. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] this is $C_i=A_i\otimes_kM$. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] to $M/E$ and $B_i=A_i\otimes_kE$. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] with $R=N=B_i$, the map $B_i\to B_i\otimes_EM\cong C_i$ is injective. A nilpotent $b\in B_i$ has zero image in this reduced $C_i$, so $b=0$. Hence every $B_i$ is reduced and steps 1 and 3 show that $X_{\bar t}$ is reduced.

For the arbitrary point $t'$, steps 4--6 establish that $X'_{\bar t'}$ is reduced exactly when $X_{\overline{g(t')}}$ is reduced. Membership in the right-hand inverse image in the statement means precisely the latter condition, so extensionality of subsets proves the asserted equality. If $Y$ is empty, the affine cover in step 3 may be empty; all its ring conditions and all local-ring reducedness conditions are vacuous, so the same argument includes empty fibres. Every use of faithful flatness was for an extension of fields, not for either of the morphisms $f$ and $g$.
